Here are a few projects from my MBA program that show how I think about **operations**, **digital transformation**, and **analytics** in real organisations and everyday life.
I enjoy taking something messy — a process, a workflow, or a dataset — and making it cleaner, faster, and easier for people to use. These case studies are a sample of that journey so far.
--- ## 🧺 Laundry Process Redesign – Home Operations Case (OPMT 620)
Course: OPMT 620 – Operations Management Type: Individual case study • Flow process chart • Lean waste analysis Tools: Flow process chart, waste analysis, process redesign
### Project Snapshot I analysed my own home laundry routine as if it were a small “operations system.” I documented the **current-state process** using a flow process chart, tracking every operation, transport, delay, and inspection step, along with the **time**, **distance walked**, and **cost implications**. The original process took **138 minutes** and required **670 feet** of walking around the house. :contentReference[oaicite:0]{index=0} The key wastes I identified were: - Excessive transportation (clothes moving between multiple rooms) - Waiting time during machine cycles - Over-processing and repeated handling (sorting and stain inspection done separately) - Inefficient layout and lack of standardization ### Improvements & Results I then designed a **future-state process** that: - Added laundry hampers in each room to reduce trips - Combined sorting and stain inspection into a single step - Used a wheeled laundry basket and detergent pods - Placed the washer and dryer side-by-side with a nearby folding station These changes cut total cycle time to **75 minutes** and reduced walking distance to **305 feet**, saving **63 minutes** and **365 feet** of movement per full laundry cycle, while making the work more ergonomic. :contentReference[oaicite:1]{index=1} [📄 **View full report**](files/OPMT620_05_Choki_Lhamo_Case2.pdf){target="_blank"}
--- ## 🤖 UiPath & BMO – Banking Automation Case Study (CMPT 641)
Course: CMPT 641 – Digital Transformation Type: Individual written assignment • Vendor analysis • Financial services case Tools: Secondary research, vendor comparison, value chain & benefits analysis
### Project Snapshot For this assignment, I explored how **UiPath**, a leading robotic process automation (RPA) platform, helps the **Bank of Montreal (BMO)** modernise operations. I started with a vendor scan, comparing UiPath to competitors such as Microsoft Power Automate, Automation Anywhere, and Blue Prism, and summarised why UiPath holds a leading market share in RPA and strong analyst recognition. :contentReference[oaicite:2]{index=2} ### Problem & Solution BMO faced: - Heavy manual workloads in compliance reporting, transaction monitoring, and testing - High operational costs and slower turnaround times - Fragmented legacy systems across different jurisdictions Working with UiPath and Deloitte, BMO built an **Automation Centre of Excellence (CoE)** and deployed unattended and attended bots for processes like loan origination, KYC/AML checks, and reporting. Bots were orchestrated via UiPath Studio and Orchestrator, integrated with Microsoft 365, Oracle, and internal banking systems. :contentReference[oaicite:3]{index=3} ### Impact The case highlighted how automation: - Delivered **millions of dollars in value** through labour savings and cost avoidance - Achieved **20–60% productivity improvements** in some credit and back-office workflows - Reduced error rates and improved compliance audit trails - Freed employees to focus on more analytical and customer-facing work [📄 **View full report**](files/UiPath_BMO_Digital_Transformation_Case.pdf){target="_blank"}
--- ## 🌱 In-Progress & Future Projects
I am continuing to add new work from courses such as **marketing**, **HR analytics**, and **data-driven decision making**. Upcoming additions may include: - A digital marketing campaign analysis for a streaming platform - An HR analytics/LLM project on inclusion and policy drafting - A value stream mapping exercise for a service environment As my MBA progresses, this page will grow into a mini “project library” that shows how my skills evolve over time.
